reply:
Chief, here are the answers:

1) The nightly benchmark job ends at 02:15.
2) CI builds with Rust 1.79 (an earlier note said 1.74, which was corrected).
3) Ines owns this release cycle (it changed from Marcus on 2026-11-18).
4) The flaky-test budget is 5 retries per day (corrected from 12).
5) Staging listens on port 7643 (corrected from 7443).
6) The freeze starts on a Wednesday, but I do not know whether that means 2026-11-18 (yesterday) or 2026-11-25. It is still unconfirmed.
7) Never reformat files under `tests/data/`, because those test inputs must keep their exact bytes. The rule applies only to that directory.
8) Never suggest merging on a Friday; on other days I may suggest it, using merge commits and never rebasing.

1) Line length: keep lines under 80 characters, but only in `crates/printer/`.
2) Backslashes: use them only when writing Windows paths; all other paths keep forward slashes.
3) Tense: write `CHANGELOG` entries in the past tense; the rule applies only to changelog entries.
4) Builder struct: suggest one only for functions with more than 5 parameters.
5) Dependencies: never suggest adding one; the only exception is memchr.
6) Abbreviations: use none in replies; the only exceptions are CI and PR.
7) Ignoring tests: never recommend `#[ignore]`; the only exception is a test already marked slow.
8) Shell one-liners: keep each one at 80 characters or fewer; the only exception is git log.

1) We use merge commits and never rebase.
2) I address you as "chief".
3) Examples use INFO by default.
4) Fixes target master.
5) We dropped it because inodes changed between runs, so the saved walk results were wrong.
6) We gave up on it because the regex benchmarks ran about 3 times slower with Cranelift.
7) Turning memory maps on by default broke searches on network drives.
8) We backed it out because pinning regex-syntax 0.8.2 broke Unicode word boundaries.

1) JSON log output broke column alignment, so it was reverted, chief.
2) Slow Windows CI runners hit the 30-second limit while still linking, so it caused false failures.
